programme.title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress [English Subtitle]
programme.sub-title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress E01 [English Subtitle]
programme.desc: At a time when the industrial revolution was carrying the world into the modern age, a horde of undead monsters suddenly appeared. They could not be killed unless their hearts, which were protected by a layer of iron, were pierced. Humans bitten by them would come back as undead monsters themselves. These undead, which would later be known as "Kabane," exploded in population until they finally overran the world. The people of Hinomoto, a nation in the far east, built fortresses known as "stations" throughout the land that have allowed them to survive the threat of the Kabane. People can only travel between these stations using fortified steam locomotives known as "Hayajiro," and they have managed to stay alive by sharing resources in this way. Ikoma is a young steamsmith living at Aragane Station, a city that specializes in the manufacture of iron and steam engines. He is working on developing a unique anti-Kabane weapon called a "piercing gun" as he waits for his chance to prove his strength. Then, one day, a Hayajiro called the "Iron Fortress" makes its way through the front lines to arrive at Aragane Station. When Ikoma begins his usual maintenance routine, he sees a mysterious girl who is exempt from her Kabane inspection. That night, Ikoma sees the girl again and learns that her name is Mumei, but then an out-of-control Hayajiro overrun by Kabane charges into Aragane Station. The Kabane pour out of the train into Aragane Station. Ikoma races against the flow of the panicked residents, this time determined not to run away, but to defeat the Kabane with his piercing gun!

programme.title: APEC Selfies: Why this ROK entrepreneur wants to call China's shoe capital home
programme.desc: Entrepreneur Michael Lee from ‪the Republic of Korea‬ came to China in 2003. More than two decades later, he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan? To become a true local! #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: Dialogue at the world's largest port: Building resilient port cities together
programme.desc: How can port cities stay resilient amid global trade uncertainty? A sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in Ningbo was held at the Ningbo Zhoushan Port — the world's No.1 port in cargo throughput for 17 straight years. CGTN's Michael Wang spoke with Ningbo's Vice Mayor and guests from Cotonou (Benin), Klang Royal City (Malaysia) and Toamasina (Madagascar). Arctic shipping routes, green corridors, sister-port cooperation — the insights keep coming!

programme.title: Smart governance, shared future: How innovation is changing our cities
programme.desc: Robots that write, grasp objects and work on real production lines are becoming an everyday reality in Ningbo. How is innovation transforming our cities? From humanoid robots and smart urban governance to balancing tourism in Florence and developing a digital city atlas in Egypt, the future is already here. Learn more at this sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in #Ningbo. #Zhejiang

programme.title: Live: Could China be the birthplace of the next global unicorn?
programme.desc: At this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), the Innovation Incubation Special Section spotlights promising startups, showcasing breakthroughs in AI, robotics, green technology, digital health, and advanced manufacturing. Under the theme "In China, Dive into New Arenas," the one-stop platform connects global startups with investors, industry leaders, and more. It also serves as a window into the upcoming APEC. Which emerging technologies could shape our future? And could the next unicorn be born here? Join CGTN's Zhu Tianlu to find out.

programme.title: How can AI and robots transform the way we receive healthcare?
programme.desc: From cutting-edge medical devices and AI-powered healthcare solutions to surgical robots changing the operating room, the latest innovations are reshaping the future of medicine at the Medical Equipment & Healthcare Products Exhibition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE). Can robots make surgery smarter and more precise? How is AI changing healthcare? Join CGTN's Bi Ran and Cao Chufeng as they explore the technologies transforming medical care.

programme.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programme.desc: Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation? Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programme.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programme.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programme.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programme.title: Biztalk Special Coverage on AI EP3
programme.desc: The Token Economy Demand for AI tokens is surging, with trends like “tokenmaxxing” accelerating the race for computing power. As pressure mounts on computing and energy infrastructure, China is leveraging its clean energy strengths to support AI growth, while “token exports” emerge as a new way to deliver AI services to global users. What’s the future like for the “token economy”? Join us on BizTalk as we explore the economics behind the AI revolution.

programme.title: COP31: From pledges to action
programme.desc: As COP31 unfolds in Türkiye, global climate action faces mounting political and economic challenges. With some major economies scaling back climate commitments and competition for green technologies intensifying, can the world turn climate pledges into action? What role can China play? Join CGTN BizTalk as leading climate experts examine the challenges facing COP31, the future of green industries, and the shifting dynamics of global climate cooperation.

programme.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programme.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: China-US: The efficiency advantage
programme.desc: The iPhone in your pocket? A global masterpiece. Apple's supply chain spans the world, with America's design expertise meeting China's manufacturing strength. Precision, speed and scale turn bold ideas into products in your hands. And this goes beyond Apple: cooperation across borders can drive innovation and growth. When the world's two biggest economies click, everyone benefits.

programme.title: RAZOR: Ghost Ponds
programme.desc: Europe has lost at least 50 percent of its ponds over the last century. Many have been filled in to make room for new developments, or drained to expand farmland. Ponds may seem like a small part of the environmental landscape, but are actually crucial to biodiversity and the fight against climate change. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi meets Professor Carl Sayer and Dr Helen Greaves from the Norfolk Ponds Project, who are on a mission to restore ponds in the UK and spark an environmental restoration. As part of an initiative backed by University College London and an EU-funded consortium called the Ponderful project, they lead expeditions to the county of Norfolk, where they aim to restore two kinds of ponds: "ghost ponds", that have either been drained or filled, and "zombie ponds" that are too overgrown and not functioning as well as they can.

programme.title: RAZOR Conversations: Sandra Diaz
programme.desc: The greatest threat facing humanity may not be climate change, but the collapse of biodiversity. The fabric of life itself, plants, animals, soils, water and ecosystems, underpins everything from the food we eat to the air we breathe. Yet that fabric is fraying at an alarming rate. Sandra Díaz, a Professor at Oxford University, is one of the world's leading ecologists and one of the most influential voices in global environmental science. An advisor to the United Nations and a key figure in international biodiversity policy, Díaz argues that biodiversity loss is not a separate environmental issue but a crisis that strikes at the foundations of human life. The damage we do to nature, she says, is ultimately damage we do to ourselves. In this episode of RAZOR: Conversations, Reya El-Salahi speaks with Díaz about why biodiversity should not be seen as something distant, confined to rainforests or endangered species, but as something intimately connected to our daily lives, economies, cultures and futures.

programme.title: BizPodcast: Why are global entrepreneurs choosing Shenzhen?
programme.desc: What makes Shenzhen such an attractive place to launch a business? With the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaching, all eyes are on this innovation-driven city in China. But beyond its reputation as a tech hub, what does it actually take to turn a big idea into a real product here? In this episode of #BizPodcast, CGTN talks with two entrepreneurs about why they chose Shenzhen, how they bring ideas to market, and what young founders should know before starting a business. Would you consider starting a business in Shenzhen? What would you want to know first?

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: How to build a digital twin of a city？
programme.desc: As cities expand and grow more intricate, a new kind of specialist is emerging behind the scenes: the urban digital twin engineer. In the coastal city of Qingdao, these experts are using real-time data and AI to build virtual replicas of the city—helping predict risks, improve infrastructure, and protect the public. CGTN's Liu Jiaxin takes us inside this fast-growing field.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: From trash to treasure
programme.desc: Jiao Jianwei is a senior engineer at the Longgang Energy Eco-Park inShenzhen. Every day, the facility processes 5,000 tonnes of waste, burning it togenerate electricity that powers millions of homes. The leftover ash is alsoturned into eco-bricks, used to pave city roads. From landfills to incineration,China has transformed its waste industry with advanced technologies. Today,the country operates more than 1,000 waste-to-energy plants – nearly half theworld's total. With national goals like "carbon neutrality" and "zero-wastecities" taking shape, engineers like Jiao are turning trash into treasure.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: Who runs China's sea-roving protein factory?
programme.desc: Ever seen "fishermen" farming salmon on a vessel with a displacement bigger than some aircraft carriers? On China's Suhai-1 – the world's first deep-sea salmon and trout aquaculture vessel – these cold-water, high-latitude fish are now thriving far from their natural habitat.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: China's Drone Show Flight Planners
programme.desc: From the skies above Chongqing, thousands of drones light up the night in dazzling displays. Behind the spectacle, a new generation of artists and engineers is redefining entertainment – and showcasing China's growing technological and economic ambitions. In this story, we take a look at the work of a drone show flight planner.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: Standing with sea giants
programme.desc: Along China's eastern shoreline, a new generation of energy workers is redefining what it meansto go to work. For offshore wind engineers, the office is the open sea. In this episode of ourspecial series Jobs 2.0, CGTN reporter Wang Tianyu takes us aboard to follow an engineer livingand working above the waves.

programme.title: Jobs 2.0: Who's teaching the robots to work?
programme.desc: As robots gradually move from research labs into real-world tasks, a key question emerges: how do machines learn to handle complex, delicate work? At a Beijing robotics company, engineers are hand-training robotic hands, translating human experience into digital skills that can be replicated at scale. CGTN's Yang Xinmeng explores this emerging profession, speaking with the people who teach machines to cook, care, and manipulate objects with precision. Their work offers a rare glimpse into the intersection of human ingenuity and artificial intelligence – and into the ways humans and robots may collaborate in everyday life.

programme.title: Mexican entrepreneur builds a China-Latin America trade bridge in the Greater Bay Area
programme.desc: Fernanda, an entrepreneur from Mexico, has launched a trade services platform in the Greater Bay Area to help Latin American companies enter the Chinese market. For her, APEC is not just a concept on paper-it is part of her everyday work, from business negotiations to cross-border partnerships. Her team also helps Chinese companies explore Latin American markets, creating new opportunities for shared growth across the Asia-Pacific.

programme.title: APEC Selfies: An Australian entrepreneur is taking AI beyond the screen. What's next?
programme.desc: From interactive smart bins to public installations that respond to emotions, Australian product designer and Sencity co-founder Steven Bai is exploring how AI can be integrated into streets, buildings and public spaces - taking technology beyond screens and into everyday life. From conceiving his startup idea to putting down roots in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, he is drawing on China's well-developed manufacturing ecosystem to bring Physical AI innovations to global markets. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: APEC Selfie: Russian creator films daily life & traditions in China's Wenzhou
programme.desc: Anna, a Chinese teacher and content creator from Russia, shares her life in Wenzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province - from experiencing local intangible cultural heritage to spending time with her family. Through these personal stories, she gives viewers abroad a glimpse of China through her eyes. Such intermingling of cultures and people-to-people exchanges are another way APEC brings the region closer.

programme.title: APEC Selfies | Brewing bridges: A Filipino entrepreneur's cross-border dream
programme.desc: What happens when a Filipino coffee lover turns his passion into a business in China? Meet Diel, founder of Nearby Coffee in Quanzhou, Fujian Province, who is serving up more than just a good brew! He's building cultural connections between China and the Philippines, with plans to take his business across borders. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: APEC Selfies: Why this ROK entrepreneur wants to call China's shoe capital home
programme.desc: Entrepreneur Michael Lee from ‪the Republic of Korea‬ came to China in 2003. More than two decades later, he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan? To become a true local! #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

programme.title: Dialogue at the world's largest port: Building resilient port cities together
programme.desc: How can port cities stay resilient amid global trade uncertainty? A sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in Ningbo was held at the Ningbo Zhoushan Port — the world's No.1 port in cargo throughput for 17 straight years. CGTN's Michael Wang spoke with Ningbo's Vice Mayor and guests from Cotonou (Benin), Klang Royal City (Malaysia) and Toamasina (Madagascar). Arctic shipping routes, green corridors, sister-port cooperation — the insights keep coming!

programme.title: Smart governance, shared future: How innovation is changing our cities
programme.desc: Robots that write, grasp objects and work on real production lines are becoming an everyday reality in Ningbo. How is innovation transforming our cities? From humanoid robots and smart urban governance to balancing tourism in Florence and developing a digital city atlas in Egypt, the future is already here. Learn more at this sub-forum of the Global Mayors Dialogue in #Ningbo. #Zhejiang

programme.title: Live: Could China be the birthplace of the next global unicorn?
programme.desc: At this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), the Innovation Incubation Special Section spotlights promising startups, showcasing breakthroughs in AI, robotics, green technology, digital health, and advanced manufacturing. Under the theme "In China, Dive into New Arenas," the one-stop platform connects global startups with investors, industry leaders, and more. It also serves as a window into the upcoming APEC. Which emerging technologies could shape our future? And could the next unicorn be born here? Join CGTN's Zhu Tianlu to find out.

programme.title: How can AI and robots transform the way we receive healthcare?
programme.desc: From cutting-edge medical devices and AI-powered healthcare solutions to surgical robots changing the operating room, the latest innovations are reshaping the future of medicine at the Medical Equipment & Healthcare Products Exhibition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE). Can robots make surgery smarter and more precise? How is AI changing healthcare? Join CGTN's Bi Ran and Cao Chufeng as they explore the technologies transforming medical care.

programme.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programme.desc: Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation? Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's concert boom: Why Gen Z is filling the stadiums

The boom now extends far beyond the stage, boosting tourism, retail spending and local economies. In this episode of Unboxing China, we explore how concerts are reshaping consumption patterns and becoming a new driver of cultural and urban development.

programme.title: The self-care economy explained: How emotional spending is reshaping consumer trends
programme.desc: For months, Chinese social feeds have been filled with "Lao Ji"- a third-person way of saying "me." What began as a slang sign-off, "Love you, Lao Ji. See you tomorrow," now signals a broader shift toward self-care and emotional self-support. It also feeds a huge market where young consumers are rechanneling budgets toward small, meaningful purchases that support emotional wellbeing. In this episode of Unboxing China, we trace how a casual phrase turned into a cultural movement, reshaping consumption and mental-health talk.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan's explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of "opening the gate", the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou's rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its "three carvings and one engraving" technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: An Encounter with China's Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father" - Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group - who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group's lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master's skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang's story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: World Heritages in Handan
programme.desc: Handan, a renowned historical and cultural city in China, boasts abundant cultural and tourism resources, including the Handan Museum and Congtai Park in Congtai District, as well as the Xiangtangshan Grottoes, Guangfu Ancient City, Cizhou Kiln, etc. Handan also has a long-standing connection with the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, a world cultural heritage. programme.title: DocFilm
programme.sub-title: Between the Czar and Hitler - The Russian Revolution and the Legacy of the White Army
programme.desc: The Russian Civil War was one of the 20th century's bloodiest chapters. The fight for Russia between Lenin's Red Army and the White Army was ruthless. Its legacy can be felt in Europe to this day.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The sun heats the Earth, and life begins again. As they prepare to breed, animals wake from hibernation and build nests in treetops and caves. Whether reptiles, birds, or mammals, all the spring babies fight for survival through their first, most challenging days.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: These are the days of thirst: it is hot. Only the mountains are cool; everywhere else suffers in heat between 40 and 50°C. The rain is long forgotten. Each day is a search for shade and water. Amphibians bury themselves in mud to escape dehydration. The rest of the wild must wait for the cool of the night to move.

programme.title: The Rhino Orphanage: The Hooligans
programme.desc: The orphanage is full. Cramped for space, the Hooligans inevitably begin to fight and Kalula is always in the thick of it. They desperately need a larger space. Karen travels to Kwa-Zulu Natal to inspect a new rhino orphanage, all part of her dream to create little ‘pockets of hope’.

programme.title: Last Devils
programme.desc: Tasmanian Devils are the world's largest carnivorous marsupials and they are only found in Tasmania. Through hundreds of hours of filming in the wild, we reveal how fights over food are a carefully choreographed ritual, we witness the seemingly brutal mating process, see tiny young developing inside their mother's pouch, and visit wild devil pups play-fighting and hunting as they prepare for life in the outside world.

programme.title: To The Ends Of The Earth
programme.desc: The rise of extreme energy, the end of economic growth, the people caught in the middle. To the Ends of the Earth is a feature documentary about the state of our energy system today, and the people we meet are uniquely positioned to watch this global crossroads unfold. For example, the mayor of an Inuit village in Canada's high Arctic who is concerned that seismic testing for oil in the ocean is blowing up the eardrums of the animals that the Inuit hunt to survive. Or the environmental lawyer who goes on a journey to areas that produce energy for the Tarsands of Alberta – he learns of the inputs of energy that have to be put into this resource - and the reasons why the second largest oil project in the world is economically unsustainable. Or the river conservationist in Utah who fights to protect the Colorado River from oil shale projects that would disturb its headwaters.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older? Through hearing their stories, we learn of some of the advantages - and disadvantages - of late-life reproduction.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In many human cultures, elders play a vital role in the well-being of communities and are responsible for passing down knowledge and culture. Is it any wonder to find that the orca, the elephant, and the wolf, have been found to transmit their respective cultures to the younger generations? Young animals learn by observing their elders. Judging when to fight or take flight, deciding how to choose a life partner, learning where to find food, these are just some of the skills passed down through the generations as elders share their wisdom.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Sao Vicente and Santo Antao
programme.desc: Sao Vicente and Santo Antao are two of the ocean-exposed islands in the often overlooked Cape Verde archipelago. The remoteness of this place has allowed natural features and wildlife to exist here that are gone from most other parts of the world.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Tofo
programme.desc: Off the coast of Mozambique's small village of Tofo, diving expeditions can yield encounters with some of the oceans greatest animals, namely, whales, orcas, manta rays, and sharks.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Sao Miguel
programme.desc: In the Azores, whales are the protagonists. Observing them, in waters covering volcanic seabeds, makes this place on of the most privileged locations for diving in the world.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Maldives
programme.desc: The Addu and Foammulah Atolls in the Maldives are home to tropical fish and vast stretches of coral reefs making diving particularly excpetional.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Komodo
programme.desc: The blend between the Pacific and Indian Oceans at Komodo Naitonal Park generates a diversity of marine flora and fauna difficult to find elsewhere. The waters house stretches of beautiful soft coral gardens and volcanic rock landscapes that leak gas from the earth’s interior.

programme.title: Top Dive Sites: Bahamas
programme.desc: Making up nearly seven hundred islands, cays, and coral reef deposits, the Bahamas boasts a diverse ecosystem made up of mangroves, swamps, and tropical flowers, but also pine forests and rocky landscapes.

programme.title: A New Prehistory
programme.desc: Today, insects are no longer giant except in our nightmares... But 320 million years ago, dragonflies measuring up to a meter (Meganeura) or centipedes the size of a human (Arthropleura) dominated the land and air. Over the course of time, these fascinating giants became smaller and smaller… before disappearing altogether. By combining state of the art scientific experiment, reconstitutions using CGI and interviews with paleontologists, stones will speak and explain why giant insects became extinct. Here is the true story of the conquest of the air.

programme.title: A New Prehistory
programme.desc: How did birds evolve? How did feathers and flight appear? After a century of silence, these questions were raised again at the beginning of the 21st century when numerous species of beautifully preserved feathered dinosaur fossils were discovered in Liaoning, China. During this paleontological investigation, each new fossil helps to complete the puzzle of the transition from dinosaurs to birds.

programme.title: A New Prehistory
programme.desc: For a long time, paleontologists believed that mammals had won the battle of evolution by default, expanding unheeded after the demise of the dinosaurs. But discoveries in China at the beginning of the 21st century prove that our ancestors prepared their weapons long before that. But exactly when did mammals first appear? For the last decade, the debate has raged between geneticists and paleontologists. Until the end of the 20th century, ancient mammals were known only through fragments of teeth but Jurassic deposits in Liaoning, China finally delivered remarkably well-preserved complete fossils: Eomaia scansoria (2002), the ancestor of placental mammals, Repenomamus giganticus (2005) the size of a dog and Volaticotherium antiquus (2006), a kind of flying squirrel. By using innovative technology such as 3D scanners scientists are able to trace the origins of their evolutionary advantages: lactation, hair, teeth and hearing. But despite these discoveries, the scientific community continued to argue over the family tree of our Mesozoic ancestors. For ten years, the debate raged between two opposing teams in the pages of the scientific publication, Nature. To understand our origins one crucial question remained unanswered: when did the now-dominant placental mammals separate from marsupials? Then in 2011, Juramaia sinensis meaning “Jurassic Mother from China” was discovered. This fossil pushed our family tree back another 35 million years, proving that our ancestors were around almost 160 million years ago…

programme.title: River Jaws
programme.desc: Wells catfish! Over the last fifty years, it has colonised most of Europe's rivers - even the most polluted. This intruder has become the largest freshwater animal in Europe, and even hunts on shore.

programme.title: Kanga Pan: An African Horror Story
programme.desc: Kanga Pan – An African Horror Story is a spine-chilling, one-off wildlife documentary, the first of its kind. A relatively unknown inland waterhole in Mana Pools National Park, Kanga Pan is a gathering point for a melting pot of wildlife species. On the surface, it looks like a peaceful oasis, offering the cooling refreshment of water and bathing.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: We follow the as they walk and stalk. Meat preparation gets weird for some as our volunteers make dinner time more interesting. A brave zebra stallion takes the fight to the ever confident lions. A historical moment is notched up for Wakanaka as she proves her predatory prowess.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: The lions attempt to dig a stubborn warthog out of his hole, while an influx of volunteers have arrived and Nathan instructs them with an induction talk on how to treat, walk and cope with lions. Laili notches up another triumph as she catches an African hare.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: We get a first peek at the adorable additions in the denning enclosure. Lewa and Laili take their hunting skills to a new level and tackle a kudu, and we find out what Rae’s doing with hyena poo! Also, Kwali takes a nasty bite to the cheek. Can she hang onto her prize?

programme.title: Wonders of the Arctic
programme.desc: Our ongoing quest to explore and come to terms with the Arctic is presented in the context of the crucial role that ice plays in the north. Ice is to the Arctic as trees are to the rainforest.

programme.title: Great White Shark - Beyond the Cage of Fear
programme.desc: Most people believe that the Great White Shark is a mindless eating machine. But what if we are wrong? In Beyond the Cage of Fear, a crew of scientists forms a relationship with a 2,000 pound Great White Shark named Bruce. They see through his eyes, swim with him, touch him and, in the end, they even attempt an experiment that most people would find absolutely crazy: introduce a Great White Shark to a real-life mermaid.

programme.title: Anaconda - The Silent Killer
programme.desc: Few snakes are feared more and understood less than the anaconda. The film shows the journey into remote and uncharted parts of the Amazon rainforest to find the truth behind the mythical beast. Lush green forests abound with colorful toucans, noisy howler monkeys, strange tapirs, and vibrant Amazon Indian tribes. But hiding in the dense vegetation and murky swamps is also the biggest and most powerful snake in the world: the anaconda.

programme.title: Mysteries of the Great Lakes
programme.desc: Through several interlocking stories including the story of maritime commerce and the ships that move cargo through the inland waterway, Mysteries of the Great Lakes will take you on a journey through the greatest lake system in the world, and showcase the amazing geography, ecology, science, and history of the region.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore how different animal species react to impending death. We explore the factors that lead animals to their final resting places: disease, injury, predation, drought, famine. Some species, such as the naked mole rat, while not immortal, seem to be able to effectively protect themselves from certain diseases such as cancer. This raises questions about what is no doubt a sensitive subject, one that brings to mind our own mortality as we speculate about the reasons for this kind of resilience in our animal counterparts. What lessons can we learn from the animal kingdom? We follow individuals to their last breath ... not as voyeurs, but as spectators attuned to the circle of life.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In this episode of Aging in the Wild, we explore the physiological secrets and factors that determine life expectancy in various animal species. From the seventy-year-old elephant to the quasi-immortal hydra, and the more than a hundred-year-old tortoise, we explore life expectancy, longevity and senescence. Can we distinguish between the effects of the environment and the internal adaptations that lead to longevity? What are some of the benefits associated with aging in nature?

programme.title: Aging in the Wild

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older? Through hearing their stories, we learn of some of the advantages - and disadvantages - of late-life reproduction.

programme.title: To The Ends Of The Earth
programme.desc: The rise of extreme energy, the end of economic growth, the people caught in the middle. To the Ends of the Earth is a feature documentary about the state of our energy system today, and the people we meet are uniquely positioned to watch this global crossroads unfold. For example, the mayor of an Inuit village in Canada's high Arctic who is concerned that seismic testing for oil in the ocean is blowing up the eardrums of the animals that the Inuit hunt to survive. Or the environmental lawyer who goes on a journey to areas that produce energy for the Tarsands of Alberta – he learns of the inputs of energy that have to be put into this resource - and the reasons why the second largest oil project in the world is economically unsustainable. Or the river conservationist in Utah who fights to protect the Colorado River from oil shale projects that would disturb its headwaters.

programme.title: Sharks: The Big Five
programme.desc: The ocean has its own Big Five. Featuring great whites, to hammerheads, tigers, bulls, and the intimidating whale shark, this is the ultimate shark show. Delve deep into the African waters and discover a new side of these prehistoric predators of the sea, while reconsidering the Hollywood portrayal which has done much to damage the reputation of these gentle creatures.

programme.title: Africa: The Serengeti
programme.desc: Chronicles a spectacle that few humans have ever witnessed, the Great Migration, taking viewers on a journey with over 1.5 million animals as they travel more than 500 miles across the Serengeti plains in Tanzania and Kenya.

programme.title: Strange Creatures of the Batangas Sea
programme.desc: Hidden in the magical underwater world of one of the most biodiverse marine areas on the planet exists a community of spectacular animals more peculiar than we can imagine.

programme.title: The Best of Worlds: Life at Its Alpine Limits
programme.desc: For 5000 years man has sought to inhabit the more accessible areas of Europe, but at its very heart, in the high zones of the Alps, there exists a world parallel to ours.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: As the woods prepare to sleep and mushrooms grow as the first rains fall, flocks of cranes migrate home to Spain from their summer season in the north. The stags clash their antlers in pursuit of the does; there is little time before winter sets in.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The unknown face of Spain. Snow, rain, clouds, and cold envelop the land. The ibex migrate to the valleys, and wolves patrol the mountains as vultures circle the skies overhead. Though the landscape looks bleak and barren at a glance, there is life thriving here.

programme.title: Wild Iberia
programme.desc: The sun heats the Earth, and life begins again. As they prepare to breed, animals wake from hibernation and build nests in treetops and caves. Whether reptiles, birds, or mammals, all the spring babies fight for survival through their first, most challenging days.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: Nicaragua, in the middle of Central America, is home to Masaya; a huge volcano that has been active for over 30,000 years. During its long life it has caused some of the largest eruptions in history. The surrounding landscape has been created from lava, ash and gas while at the centre lies a desolate, empty land. Each time the Masaya volcano destroys everything around it, life returns, re-emerging from the ash at its fee

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In the vast emptiness of the Pacific Ocean, tectonic movements construct or destroy islands. In the Tongan archipelago, two little-known animals have learnt to cope with these ephemeral lands: the sooty tern, a seabird that never dares wet its wings for fear of drowning and the Alvin shrimp, a blind crustacean that nonetheless manages to find its way around the abyss. When an underwater volcano becomes an island, the fates of these two living paradoxes are linked.

programme.title: Life On Fire
programme.desc: In 2010, the eruption of the Eyjafjallajokull volcano in Iceland provoked a vast economic chaos by paralysing one of the world's major air traffic networks for several days. Through spectacular aerial footage, the film tries to understand which volcano could wake up next and what the consequences of a major eruption are likely to be. The world has come to realize that a colossal power sleeps beneath Iceland but Icelanders have learned to live amongst their volcanoes for centuries.

programme.title: Anaconda - The Silent Killer
programme.desc: Few snakes are feared more and understood less than the anaconda. The film shows the journey into remote and uncharted parts of the Amazon rainforest to find the truth behind the mythical beast. Lush green forests abound with colorful toucans, noisy howler monkeys, strange tapirs, and vibrant Amazon Indian tribes. But hiding in the dense vegetation and murky swamps is also the biggest and most powerful snake in the world: the anaconda.

programme.title: Leopard Seals, Lords of the Ice
programme.desc: Göran Ehlmé, a naturalist and specialist in cold water diving, is haunted by the memory of a terrible encounter with a still unknown predator, a seal that looks like an ogre: the sea leopard. A giant seal that lives on the edge of the planet in the most inhospitable place there is: Antarctica, a world of ice and rock. Göran sets out to meet this super predator to unlock some of its secrets. He witnesses a dramatic face-to-face encounter between several leopard seals and a colony of penguins, a unique opportunity to see and film unprecedented hunting behaviour.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: Penya and Paza encounter a python; the adorable cubs go on their first bush outing; Lewa and Laili keep the zebra on their toes. Meanwhile, the research team have more experiments for the Ngamo lions.

programme.title: Roaring With Pride
programme.desc: The lions are on the hunt for giraffe. Meanwhile, researcher Rae accompanies the lions as they encounter nervy hartebeest. The game capture unit are tasked with supplying more zebra for the Ngama release site. And don’t miss the action as hungry Kwali zones in on an unsuspecting zebra. But can she hold on?

programme.title: Turtle Odyssey
programme.desc: Sea turtles are some of Earth's most ancient and majestic creatures. For over 100 million years, they have traversed the seas, enduring mass extinctions and playing critical roles in maintaining food webs. But now they face a new threat – humans. It's time we learned more about these remarkable reptiles.

programme.title: Pharm to Table
programme.desc: How far would you go, to know what's in your food? As we go about our daily lives, few of us stop to wonder what our food is really made of. Taylor Lancastor travels 2800 miles on foot, to defend our right to know, and discover the truth of what we are being fed.

programme.title: Secret Seychelles: D’Arros
programme.desc: D'Arros is one of the Seychelles' best kept secrets. Safe-guarded by isolation, the island is a jewel of the Indian Ocean. Teaming with wildlife, the sand cay and neighbouring coral atoll are home to rare giant tortoises, hawksbill turtles, and shearwaters. In the depths, dolphins, greater hammerhead and tiger sharks roam. Green turtles nest on the pristine beaches, reef sharks bear live pups in the shallow lagoon, whales come to the deep channel, and mantas feed over coral reefs. Now designated as a wildlife reserve this natural treasure trove has the recognition it so rightly deserves.

programme.title: Japan: The Sense of Season
programme.desc: In this episode, we delve into the spring and summer months. Spring is a time of fleeting beauty as Japan’s famous cherry blossom drifts across the nation and wild visitors welcome the warming conditions. As spring rolls into summer, dramatic festivals, mysterious animals and seasonal harvests spark into life right across Japan’s islands and coastal waters.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: Aging in the Wild
programme.desc: In many human cultures, elders play a vital role in the well-being of communities and are responsible for passing down knowledge and culture. Is it any wonder to find that the orca, the elephant, and the wolf, have been found to transmit their respective cultures to the younger generations? Young animals learn by observing their elders. Judging when to fight or take flight, deciding how to choose a life partner, learning where to find food, these are just some of the skills passed down through the generations as elders share their wisdom.

programme.desc: With an all-star cast that includes Sean Connery, Anthony Hopkins, Laurence Olivier, Gene Hackman and Robert Redford, this epic WW II drama recreates Operation Market Garden, an ambitious plan to hasten the end of WW II that ended in disaster.

programme.title: Red Dawn (2025)
programme.desc: The invasion has begun! Patrick Swayze, C. Thomas Howell, Lea Thompson and Charlie Sheen wage unremitting guerilla warfare in defense of their parents, their friends, their town and their country when Communist invaders storm their hometown.

programme.title: Navy Seals (1990)
programme.desc: Charlie Sheen, Michael Biehn and Bill Paxton are three of America's finest Navy commandos. Sent to rescue the crew of a U.S. aircraft carrying Stinger missiles seized by Mideast terrorists, they're thrust onto the frontline of an explosive conflict!

programme.title: Enter The Ninja (2023)
programme.desc: When Cole (Franco Nero), a westerner trained in the deadly fighting rituals of Ninjitsu, is suddenly dragged into a dangerous dispute with an oil baron, he must face the best assassin money can buy, Ninja Hasegawa (martial arts legend Sho Kosugi)!

programme.title: Revenge Of The Ninja (2023)
programme.desc: When a band of Ninja assassins slaughters the family of Cho Osaki (Sho Kosugi), he flees to America in the hope of building a new life. Osaki tries to escape his deadly past but soon discovers he has become the pawn of a ruthless drug trafficker.

programme.title: Ninja III: The Domination (2023)
programme.desc: Possessed by the spirit of a diabolical Ninja assassin and dominated by his relentless rage, a young, attractive woman sets out to brutally attack and destroy his enemies. Can her boyfriend and a martial arts master possibly save her soul?

programme.title: Hercules (2014) (2026)
programme.desc: Dwayne Johnson stars as the most towering myth of all time, revealing the man behind the legend in this bold reimaging of the famed Hercules!

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: July 1943 to December 1943. On daylight bombing missions, American airmen gamble with their lives against overwhelming odds to bring the war to the heart of Hitler's vast empire. Allied forces invade Sicily and then Italy but, as they grind their way towards Rome, the weather turns bad and the terrain grows more and more forbidding. Twisting mountain roads and blown bridges have to be negotiated while under constant German fire. A series by Ken Burns. Part 4 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: November 1943 to February 1944. In November, the US marines take the tiny Pacific atoll of Tarawa, but at a terrible cost. Back home, Japanese-Americans are permitted to form a special segregated infantry unit and begin to train for combat. As the war economy booms, ugly racial violence erupts in cities across the country. Overseas, in the mountains south of Rome, the allies try to fight their way around the edges of Monte Cassino, but are stopped cold. A series by Ken Burns. Part 5 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1944 to June 1944. American and British troops are pinned down at Anzio for months, while at Monte Cassino, the killing goes on and on. African-Americans, incensed at the segregation of the armed forces, put pressure on the military to make some changes. In May, allied soldiers at Cassino and Anzio resume their drive northward in Italy, liberating Rome on 4 June, but they let the retreating German army get away. A series by Ken Burns. Part 6 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: 6 June 1944: D-Day. In the early hours of 6 June 1944, the invasion of France begins. A million-and-a-half men take part. It is the bloodiest day in American history since the Civil War, though the Allies succeed in tearing a 45-mile gap in Hitler's vaunted Atlantic Wall. By day's end more than 150,000 men have landed on French soil, and more men, equipment and supplies are coming ashore every hour. A series by Ken Burns. Part 7 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: June 1944 to August 1944. American and British troops in Normandy are bogged down in the hedgerows, while in the Pacific, the marines fight their costliest battle to date on the island of Saipan. Back home, dreaded telegrams from the War Department begin arriving at a rate inconceivable just one year earlier. But by mid-August, the Germans are in full retreat out of France, and on 25 August, after four years of Nazi occupation, Paris is liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 8 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In September of 1944, with their troops in Europe stalled on the German border having outrun their supply lines, Allied commanders gamble on a risky plan to drop thousands of airborne troops behind enemy lines in Holland. When the mission ends in disaster, it becomes painfully clear that the war in Europe will not end before winter. In the Pacific, on the island of Peleliu, the marines fight one of the most brutal campaigns of the war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 9 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: December 1941 to March 1942. The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941 thrusts the United States into the global cataclysm that will eventually touch every family on every street in every town in America. Within a few months, millions of young men have entered the armed forces and are beginning to train for war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 1 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: March 1942 to December 1942. With U-boats menacing the East Coast, and little good news from overseas, many worry that the United States is utterly unprepared to fight in a 'total war'. But after six months of gruelling combat on Guadalcanal, the Americans finally stop Japan's expansion in the Pacific. A series by Ken Burns. Part 2 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: January 1943 to June 1943. American troops land in North Africa and test themselves for the first time against the German and Italian armies, learning to set aside the notion that killing is a sin, and adopting the outlook that 'killing is a craft'. Back home, cities become booming 'war towns' overnight as nearly all manufacturing is converted to the war effort, and thousands of women become industrial workers. A series by Ken Burns. Part 3 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In the late autumn of 1944 American soldiers suffer terrible losses when they are ordered into the forbidding and fiercely defended terrain of the Hrtgen Forest and the Vosges Mountains. In the Central Pacific, to the delight of audiences back home, General MacArthur returns to the island of Leyte. But months of bloody fighting lie ahead before the Philippine Islands, and the people imprisoned on them, can be liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 10 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter 1944 to 1945. The Allies are unprepared for Hitler's counterattack in the Ardennes Forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. It is the biggest battle of the war on the Western Front, fought during the coldest winter in memory. By the time the Battle of the Bulge is over, Hitler's enormous gamble has ended in disaster and the Russians are approaching Berlin. Meanwhile, in the Santo Tomas Camp in the Philippines, thousands of internees await liberation. A series by Ken Burns. Part 11 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter to Spring 1945. On the island of Iwo Jima, the marines face 21,000 Japanese defenders who, without hope of reinforcement, have been ordered to kill as many Americans as possible before being killed themselves. Once the island is taken, Allied bombers set the cities of Japan ablaze, killing thousands and leaving millions homeless. In Europe, Americans are crossing the Rhine and driving into Germany, while the Russians are within 50 miles of Berlin. A series by Ken Burns. Part 12 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Spring 1945. In the Pacific, Americans fight on the island of Okinawa while kamikaze pilots wreak havoc on the fleet offshore. In Europe, allied forces rapidly push across Germany from the east and west, and American and British troops discover the true horrors of the Nazis' industrialised barbarism at Buchenwald, Dachau, Mauthausen and other concentration camps. Finally, on 8 May, with their country in ruins and their Fuhrer dead, the Germans surrender. A series by Ken Burns. Part 13 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: May to December 1945. In June, the battle on Okinawa ends yet Japan's rulers, despite the agony their people are enduring, resist unconditional surrender. On 6 August 1945, an American plane drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. Two days later, Russia declares war against Japan. A second atomic bomb is dropped on Nagasaki and, finally, Japan surrenders. In the following months, hundreds of thousands of American servicemen and women return home. A series by Ken Burns. Part 14 of 14.

But by mid-August, the Germans are in full retreat out of France, and on 25 August, after four years of Nazi occupation, Paris is liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 8 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In September of 1944, with their troops in Europe stalled on the German border having outrun their supply lines, Allied commanders gamble on a risky plan to drop thousands of airborne troops behind enemy lines in Holland. When the mission ends in disaster, it becomes painfully clear that the war in Europe will not end before winter. In the Pacific, on the island of Peleliu, the marines fight one of the most brutal campaigns of the war. A series by Ken Burns. Part 9 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Autumn 1944. In the late autumn of 1944 American soldiers suffer terrible losses when they are ordered into the forbidding and fiercely defended terrain of the Hrtgen Forest and the Vosges Mountains. In the Central Pacific, to the delight of audiences back home, General MacArthur returns to the island of Leyte. But months of bloody fighting lie ahead before the Philippine Islands, and the people imprisoned on them, can be liberated. A series by Ken Burns. Part 10 of 14.

programme.title: The War
programme.desc: Winter 1944 to 1945. The Allies are unprepared for Hitler's counterattack in the Ardennes Forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. It is the biggest battle of the war on the Western Front, fought during the coldest winter in memory. By the time the Battle of the Bulge is over, Hitler's enormous gamble has ended in disaster and the Russians are approaching Berlin. Meanwhile, in the Santo Tomas Camp in the Philippines, thousands of internees await liberation. A series by Ken Burns. Part 11 of 14.

programme.title: Eliminators

programme.title: Meet the Spartans

programme.title: The Competition
programme.desc: Lauren Mauldin (Thora Birch) is a strong-willed but misguided young woman who encourages her millions of blog followers to apply her scientific formula to all romantic relationships in order to prevent heartache.

programme.title: Gambit
programme.desc: Harry Deane is a man with a plan. Art curator for media tycoon Lord Lionel Shahbandar, Harry devises an elaborate plot to con Shahbandar into purchasing a fake Monet painting.\r.

programme.title: Bite Me
programme.desc: When Sarah, a real-life vampire, gets audited by the IRS, the last thing she expects to get out of it is a date. But James, her hopelessly romantic IRS agent, thinks she’s other-worldly.

programme.title: Black Knight
programme.desc: The Middle Ages may never be the same after street smart Jamal Walker falls into a moat at the Medieval World theme park and finds himself transported back in time.

programme.title: Double Trouble
programme.desc: Two Brazilian billionaires hire a pair of look-alikes to temporarily take their place and find out who is trying to assassinate them.

programme.title: Ruth & Alex
programme.desc: When Ruth and Alex opt to put their apartment on the market over one crazy weekend, they discover that finding a new apartment is not about winding down..

programme.title: Dog Days
programme.desc: “What is it about dogs that brings us so much joy?” Lives are about to change forever, when human and canine paths intertwine in sunny Los Angeles. There’s Elizabeth, a news anchor in her 30’s, who not only having to deal with a bad breakup, is struggling to cheer up her depressed dog Sam.

programme.title: Girl Asleep
programme.desc: The world is closing in on Greta Driscoll. On the cusp of turning fifteen she can't bear to leave her childhood, it contains all the things that give her comfort in this incomprehensible new world.

programme.title: I Feel Pretty
programme.desc: A woman struggling with insecurity wakes from a fall believing she is the most beautiful woman on the planet. Her new confidence empowers her to live fearlessly, but what happens when she realizes her appearance never changed.

programme.title: Things Like This
programme.desc: When two guys with the same name start falling in love it seems like everything has aligned for them to be together. But is fate ever exactly how you expect it to be.

programme.title: Standing Up for Sunny
programme.desc: An isolated guy with cerebral palsy is railroaded into helping an unassertive comedienne, and finds love and acceptance through stand up comedy.

programme.title: Senior Moment
programme.desc: Stripped of his driver's license, a retired NASA pilot must not only battle with the DMV, he must find new ways to navigate love and life without his beloved vintage Porsche.

programme.title: Holy Water
programme.desc: A rural Irish village will never be the same again after a group of bachelors hijack a truck full of Viagra pills as part of a get-rich-quick scheme. With special ops on their case, the boys hide the loot down the Church's Holy Well... only for it to seep out into the town's water supply.

programme.title: Zookeeper
programme.desc: In this warm-hearted comedy, the animals at one particular zoo love their caretaker, Griffin Keyes (Kevin James). But when Griffin decides the only way he can get a girl in his life is to find a more glamorous job, the animals, in a panic, break their time-honored code of silence..

programme.title: Cooking with Love
programme.desc: Hardworking & optimistic television producer, Kelly, doesn’t have time for love. Along with her mentor Amanda, Kelly dives into another season of the Little Gourmet, a kids cooking show, when hot-headed Chef Stephen is dropped into Kelly’s life as a last minute replacement host.

programme.title: Big Mommas: Like Father, Like Son
programme.desc: Big Momma is back — and this time he has big backup: his teenage stepson Trent (Brendan T. Jackson). Martin Lawrence returns as FBI agent Malcolm Turner and as Turner’s deep-cover alter-ego Big Momma.

programme.title: Riddle of Fire
programme.desc: In the rolling hills of Wyoming, three mischievous children are tasked with collecting a blueberry pie from their local store.

programme.title: 36 Husbands
programme.desc: 36 Husbands is a mystical, musical, Kung Fu spy comedy starring 3 powerful women - and a bunch of husbands. Krista, top spy and Kung Fu master, has extraordinary powers and she puts them in action on her quest to slow down the steady march towards World War III.

programme.title: Overboard
programme.desc: Unjustly fired by a spoilt and selfish yacht owner, Kate gets payback when he falls overboard and wakes up with amnesia..

programme.title: All for Love
programme.desc: When an engaged romance novelist is teamed with a Navy man as research for her latest book, she is taken aback by his boisterous personality and egotistical nature.

programme.title: She's Funny That Way
programme.desc: Isabella, a young Hollywood starlet, recalls how the actions of charming Broadway director, Arnold, changed her life forever.

programme.title: The Winning Season
programme.desc: Sam Rockwell and fast rising star Emma Roberts, comes the hilarious story of a washed up basketball coach who must learn to overcome his love of booze.

programme.title: The Pink Panther
programme.desc: When a star soccer coach is murdered and his priceless Pink Panther diamond stolen, France is in an uproar. Fortunately, Inspector Jacques Clouseau (Steve Martin) is on the case with his trusted partner Gilbert Ponton (Jean Reno). Will he seduce the pop diva, Xania (Beyoncé Knowles).

programme.title: Camp
programme.desc: A coming-of-age story centered around a group of teenagers who navigate friendship, romance, and betrayal in their final year of sleep-away camp.

programme.title: Language Lessons
programme.desc: When Adam's (Mark Duplass) husband surprises him with weekly Spanish lessons, he's unsure about where or how this new element will fit into his already structured life.

programme.title: Apocalypse Clown
programme.desc: A global technology blackout plunges Ireland into chaos. In a world where social media and vloggers are a thing of the past, a group of washed up clowns use the impending apocalypse to chase their dreams.

programme.title: A Boy Called Po
programme.desc: After his wife dies of cancer, an overworked engineer struggles to care for his son with autism. His son in response to bullying regresses into a fantasy world escape.

programme.title: Bee Season
programme.desc: Richard Gere stars in this gripping tale about a father obsessed with training his talented daughter for the National Spelling Bee.

programme.title: After The Wedding
programme.desc: Isabel (Michelle Williams) has devoted her life to running an orphanage in a Kolkata slum. With funds running dry, she lands uncomfortably in the sights of a possible benefactor, Theresa Young (Julianne Moore), a multi-millionaire media mogul. Theresa's life couldn't appear to be more perfect.

programme.title: Loving Vincent
programme.desc: Vincent Willem van Gogh is undoubtedly one of the most famous and influential figures in the history of Western art. Yet during his lifetime Vincent struggled with poverty and depression, dying at only 37 years old.

programme.title: The Man Without a Face
programme.desc: A drama film about a young boy who befriends a disfigured recluse in a small coastal town; and helps him overcome his fear of society and confront his past.

programme.title: Please Stand By
programme.desc: A young autistic woman runs away from her caregiver to boldly go and deliver her 500-page Star Trek script to a writing competition in Hollywood. On an adventure full of laughter and tears, Wendy follows the guiding spirit of Mr. Spock on her journey into the unknown.

programme.title: A Hologram for the King
programme.desc: A Hologram for the King follows businessman Alan Clay (Tom Hanks) on a journey halfway around the world, far from his American roots, to a rising Saudi Arabian city.

programme.title: A Rainy Day in New York
programme.desc: Woody Allen’s romantic comedy A RAINY DAY IN NEW YORK tells the story of college sweethearts, Gatsby (Timothée Chalamet) and Ashleigh (Elle Fanning), whose plans for a romantic weekend together in New York City are dashed as quickly as the sunlight turns into showers.

programme.title: On a Wing and a Prayer
programme.desc: In this extraordinary true story of faith and survival, "On A Wing and A Prayer" follows passenger Doug White’s (Dennis Quaid) harrowing journey to safely land a plane and save his entire family from insurmountable danger after their pilot dies unexpectedly mid-flight. Heather Graham also stars.

programme.title: Noah
programme.desc: Academy Award® winner Russell Crowe stars as Noah, a man chosen by God for a great task before an apocalyptic flood destroys the world.

programme.title: Bravetown
programme.desc: Josh is a lost soul with an extraordinary musical talent set on a journey to encounter what he was least expecting but undoubtedly needed most.

programme.title: Gangland Revenge
programme.desc: After his son is killed in a gang hit, a father must protect his broken family and seek justice. Drawing on his past as a fighter, he enters the brutal gangland underworld to take down his son’s killers. Gangland Revenge is a tense British crime thriller.

programme.title: Life at These Speeds
programme.desc: After a teenager's friends are killed in an accident, he finds running allows him to remember them perfectly. Running, however, also brings him notoriety. Soon he finds himself caught between keeping the past alive and making new memories in the present.

programme.title: The Way Back
programme.desc: The Way Back is the critically acclaimed new release from renowned director Peter Weir (Master and Commander, The Truman Show), starring Colin Farrell, Jim Sturgess, Ed Harris, Mark Strong and Saoirse Ronan.

programme.title: The Ark
programme.desc: The Ark is a retelling of the biblical story of Noah and The Ark. Noah, a farmer and family man, is instructed by an angel to build an ark in the middle of a desert in order to save both his family and the faithful from a devastating flood.

programme.title: Love Sarah
programme.desc: Three generations of women, led by Mimi will need to overcome grief, doubts and differences to honour the memory of their beloved Sarah, while embarking on a journey to establish a new bakery in Notting Hill, a place filled with love, hope and colourful pastries from all over the world.

programme.title: Rex
programme.desc: Rex is based on the true-life story of young Marine Corporal Megan Leavey whose unique discipline and bond with her military combat dog saved many lives during their deployment in Iraq.

programme.title: Freeheld
